sentences.text: This study investigated radiation-induced brain injury, a condition affecting up to 30% of patients receiving head radiation, by testing a new nanomaterial on mice that had received a specific dose of whole-body radiation equal to 6 grays.

Using electrical recordings inside living animals, researchers found that the treatment helped restore the electrical activity of specific brain cells and improved the animals' movement and anxiety levels while also protecting other organs and allowing all treated mice to survive for 30 days.
The authors suggest that fixing how neurons fire electrically is a new and promising way to treat radiation brain injury, though these results were observed only in mice.
